IR.rationale: Rising intermediate yields relative to the policy rate erode the duration component of both indices and signal expected tightening, which pushes capital out of EM dollar debt.

B.rationale: Strong high-yield returns together with stable or narrowing Baa spreads mark easy credit conditions. Credit returns are positively autocorrelated because of illiquidity and slow capital flows.

V.rationale: Elevated equity implied volatility proxies for a high price of risk, which predicts higher subsequent risk premia in risky credit.

AP.rationale: Equities lead corporate and EM bonds because credit prices adjust more slowly to news about firm and sovereign value. Joint US and EM equity strength therefore signals improving credit fundamentals.

ST.rationale: Equity style factors carry little direct information about credit index returns beyond the market factor.

FX.rationale: Dollar strength tightens global dollar funding and worsens EM sovereigns' external debt burdens, which weighs on dollar-denominated EM and risky credit.

COM.rationale: Energy issuers are a large share of US high yield, and many EM sovereigns are oil exporters, so oil price moves feed through to default risk and spreads.

MC.rationale: Tight financial conditions mean constrained intermediaries and elevated required returns on credit, which carries information about subsequent returns.

ENDG.rationale: High-yield and EM bond index returns show short-horizon momentum, owing to stale pricing and gradual flows.

IR.rationale: Abrupt rises in intermediate yields over the policy rate signal policy repricing, which raises duration and flow-driven volatility in dollar credit.

B.rationale: Widening spreads combined with weak high-yield returns identify a credit stress state, and volatility clusters and rises in such states.

V.rationale: High implied volatility in equities and oil anticipates turbulence that spills into high-yield and EM spreads, especially through energy and commodity exposure.

AP.rationale: Leverage and volatility-feedback effects mean that equity declines, particularly joint US and EM declines, raise future volatility of risky assets.

ST.rationale: High returns to short-term reversal reflect high returns to liquidity provision, which occur when liquidity is scarce and markets are volatile.

FX.rationale: Yen appreciation together with Australian dollar weakness marks a carry-trade unwind and risk-off deleveraging, which raises cross-asset volatility.

COM.rationale: Oil price falls raise default risk for energy high-yield issuers and oil-exporting sovereigns, increasing spread volatility.

MC.rationale: Elevated financial stress indicates fragile funding and liquidity, which amplifies subsequent price swings in credit.

ENDG.rationale: Very high recent variance captures nonlinear volatility persistence beyond the linear baseline.

IR.rationale: Sharp repricing of intermediate yields raises the risk of duration losses and outflows from EM dollar debt.

B.rationale: Widening spreads with falling high-yield prices signal a deteriorating credit state in which forced selling and illiquidity produce tail losses.

V.rationale: High implied volatility widens the return distribution and raises crash probabilities for risky assets.

AP.rationale: Equity weakness leads credit repricing, so recent equity losses raise the probability of a subsequent large credit loss.

ST.rationale: High reversal-factor returns indicate scarce liquidity, a condition under which credit drawdowns deepen.

FX.rationale: A surging dollar tightens global funding and pressures EM sovereign creditworthiness, raising tail-loss risk.

COM.rationale: Oil price declines hit energy-heavy high yield and oil-exporting sovereigns, raising the chance of large losses.

MC.rationale: Tight financial conditions reflect intermediary balance-sheet constraints that make fire-sale losses more likely.

ENDG.rationale: Poor recent returns signal an ongoing sell-off, and loss streaks persist in illiquid credit markets.

IR.rationale: Falling intermediate yields, from easing expectations, produce duration gains and draw inflows into credit and EM debt.

B.rationale: Strong high-yield returns with narrowing spreads indicate a credit rally that tends to persist across weeks.

V.rationale: Large gains cluster in high-volatility, high-risk-premium states, as rebounds follow dislocations.

AP.rationale: Broad US and EM equity rallies lead improvements in credit and sovereign spreads.

ST.rationale: Momentum losses typically occur in sharp junk rebounds after stress, which coincide with large credit rallies.

FX.rationale: A weakening dollar eases global funding and EM debt burdens, supporting large gains in EM and high-yield bonds.

COM.rationale: Oil rallies reduce default risk for energy issuers and oil exporters, producing sharp spread tightening.

MC.rationale: Large rebounds come out of stressed states, when risk premia are highest and mean reversion is strongest.

ENDG.rationale: Strong recent returns signal a rally regime, and positive autocorrelation in credit returns raises the chance of continued large gains.
